chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, who said: Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Fudayl ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him)

He said: A group of people entered his presence, those who speak about Lordship (al-Rububiyyah). He said to them: Fear Allah and revere Allah, and do not say what we do not say. For if you say one thing and we say another, then you will die and we will die. Then Allah will raise you, and He will raise us, and you will be where Allah wills, and we will be.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advise regarding discussing Allah's Lordship?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the Shia principle of *al-ittiba'* (following the Imams) in theological discourse, warning against speculative debates on *Rububiyyah* that diverge from established Imamate teachings. The Imam emphasizes that doctrinal deviation leads to spiritual death and subsequent divine judgment, underscoring the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt as the definitive interpreters of divine attributes.
